notes.C01: Strong idea for the re-voice job, but it couples two tools and needs a calibration harness before any check can act, and every dub gets re-sensed.
notes.C02: Directly targets the 'reads like English' dub pace with signals mediasift already has; it only helps dubbing.
notes.C03: Stops wrong speech from feeding fact-checks and summaries without hiding it, which matches crash-over-corrupt; the escalation budget adds some compute.
notes.C04: Well aimed at fact-checking and sensibly kept off the default card, but the second-backend re-hearing and the witness logic add machinery for a job that is used rarely.
notes.C05: Uses the most common real input (captioned reels) to get a free Vietnamese judge and possibly skip the 3.3 GB MLX pass, and the first test is concrete.
notes.C06: The credit line is cheap and useful, but the fingerprint morgue covers a cache that is almost all bench runs and adds network peeks and a store that keeps growing.
notes.C07: Answers the most-repeated real ask (link several videos with citations), at the cost of an index that has to stay in sync with the cache.
notes.C08: Real token savings, but the rent ledger, leases and crossover curve are knobs that need retuning, and deleting the long-media timeline is risky.
notes.C09: Gives the judge gate a real source of labels, but many harvesters, leases and monthly audits are a standing burden to run.
notes.C10: Fixes a real defect (733 dead commands) and makes partial senses honest; cheap, concrete and testable, though not new.
notes.C11: A clever cue sheet, but the owner's jobs rarely need editorial music detail, and it adds card lines with no measured question behind them.
notes.C12: A tidy roster that cuts tokens and serves citing and casting; name binding depends on witnesses that short reels often lack.
notes.C13: Nearly free and fully judgeable, but it helps only a niche part of dubbing.
